title: Theo Thinks His FSA Rolls Over Forever 😂
description:
Theo has $2,000 left in his FSA and is sure it rolls over forever. Nora explains he's mixing it up with an HSA: an FSA is use it or lose it. If his plan allows a carryover, only $680 moves into next year. The other $1,320 is forfeited after the plan deadline. Theo's answer? A hundred bottles of sunscreen.

Takeaway: an HSA balance rolls over year after year; an FSA mostly doesn't. Check your plan's deadline and, at open enrollment, put in roughly what you'll actually spend.

Got an FSA? Do you know your deadline? Tell us below 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Illustration with a hypothetical Theo who put in the 2026 maximum and spent $1,400. Figures: 2026 health FSA limit $3,400 and maximum carryover $680 (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32). Plans can offer a carryover, a grace period of up to 2.5 months, or neither, so check your own plan's rules. This is not financial advice.
